questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation to keep riders together while leaving enough space between them?

options.text: Single-file formation.
Riding in pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of riders to stay close together while giving each rider enough space to ride safely.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent this damage.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:

options.text: A lack of oil.
A lack of fuel.
Improper tire inflation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lack of oil.
questions.explanation: Without enough oil, the engine's parts cannot move smoothly. The engine overheats and seizes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you pass an emergency scene.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog approach, and then speed up to get away.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog approach, and then speed up to get away.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and let it get close. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Your arms should steer, not hold you up. Your elbows should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load high on a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects its balance.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid talking or moving unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking or moving unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should board after the engine starts and sit as far forward as possible without bothering the rider.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after finishing a turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: How long will your license be suspended for a first DUI offense?

options.text: 10 days.
20 days.
30 days.
90 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 90 days.
questions.explanation: For a first DUI offense, your license will be suspended for 90 days.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you on the left?

options.text: Speed up.
Stay in the right part of your lane.
Stay in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, stay in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side of your lane can be unsafe because it may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles will protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields will not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What should be part of your normal scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.
Check your rearview mirror often.
Do not use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirror frequently as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance a motorcyclist should maintain under normal conditions?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. When conditions are not ideal, use a larger following distance.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?

options.text: Always ride single-file.
It depends on the situation.
Always ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: In most cases, ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols or text. This warning sign tells you that a divided roadway is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow traffic light warns you that the light is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: What is the best way to cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight across within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight across within your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks is to ride straight across within your lane. Changing your angle to cross the tracks may move you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look where you want to go.
Turn your head and shoulders to look where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level. Turning your shoulders can make you steer wrong.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger handles differently because of the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more time to stop. The passenger should hold onto the passenger grips or the rider's waist firmly and securely.

questions.question: If you cannot see 100 feet ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder.
Follow another vehicle to use as a guide.
Ride at a slightly slower speed.
Pull over and wait for the conditions to improve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and wait for the conditions to improve.
questions.explanation: It is unsafe to ride if you cannot see at least 100 feet ahead. Pull off the road and wait until conditions improve before continuing.

questions.question: A sign that your front tire has gone flat is that your steering suddenly feels:

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.
